record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.context_brief: rational periodic points for maps with parameter δ
record.original_question: For all but finitely many δ∈Q, do all Q-rational periodic points of maps f(x,y)=(y,y^2+c−δx) with c∈Q have period dividing 2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4. — For all but finitely many δ ∈ Q, the Q-rational periodic points of any f(x, y) = (y, y2 + c − δx) with c ∈ Q have period dividing 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a rational parameter pair $(c,\delta)\in\mathbb{Q}^2$, consider the polynomial automorphism of the affine plane
$$f_{c,\delta}\colon \mathbb{A}^2\to\mathbb{A}^2,\qquad f_{c,\delta}(x,y)=(y,\;y^2+c-\delta x).$$
A point $P\in\mathbb{Q}^2$ is called a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational periodic point of $f_{c,\delta}$ if there exists an integer $n\geq 1$ such that $f_{c,\delta}^{\circ n}(P)=P$; the smallest such $n$ is the (exact) period of $P$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a finite set $S\subset\mathbb{Q}$ such that for every $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus S$ and every $c\in\mathbb{Q}$, every $\mathbb{Q}$-rational periodic point of $f_{c,\delta}$ has period dividing $2$ (i.e., period equal to $1$ or $2$).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in a recent list of open problems on Hénon maps and is stated explicitly as Conjecture 4. A 2024 preprint constructs Hénon maps over Q of odd degree d with many integral periodic points and integer cycles of large period, giving evidence about uniform boundedness but not resolving the dividing-by-2 conjecture for the specific family f(x,y)=(y, y^2+c-δx). No proof or disproof appears in the located literature, so the problem is considered open.

status_evidence.title: Hénon maps with many rational periodic points
status_evidence.snippet: For each odd integer d ≥ 2 a Hénon map of degree d defined over Q with at least (d-4)^2 integral periodic points... examples also admit integer cycles of large period.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work produces Hénon maps with many rational periodic points and large period cycles, but does not resolve the specific conjecture for f(x,y)=(y, y^2+c-δx).
